label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their mean scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale (1.74), PHQ-9 depression scale (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety scale (2.17) all fall in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of emotional distress across multiple dimensions. The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education may reflect individuals in demanding academic or professional environments who experience significant psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating perceived social isolation despite likely digital connectivity
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ~1.75) suggesting persistent low mood and functional impact
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean ~2.17) pointing to frequent worry and tension
Heavy daily screen use (>5 hours) potentially reflecting both occupational demands and coping-related digital engagement
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional distress
tone: Burdened and emotionally strained, reflecting a pattern of quiet struggle beneath high-functioning daily routines

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near the low end of the scale)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours)
Demonstrates a consistent pattern of low psychological distress across all assessed domains

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the emotional distress patterns typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping mechanisms that buffer against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) well below clinical thresholds
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) suggesting minimal worry or nervousness
Relatively limited daily screen time (1–3 hours), possibly reflecting disciplined digital habits
Disconnect between social isolation feelings and affective symptom severity
tone: Quietly detached yet emotionally stable; reflective rather than distressed
